title: Derived pullback of ringed topoi carries canonical SES triangles of flat-term K-flat complexes to canonical triangles
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small relative to the universe of the module sheaves, with sheaves of commutative rings $R$ on $\mathcal C$ and $S$ on $\mathcal D$, and let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a morphism of topoi, an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits, equipped with a ring map $c:u^{-1}R\to S$. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] put $u^*M=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], applied termwise to cochain complexes. Let $Q_R,Q_S$ be the derived-category localizations with their shift isomorphisms $Q(K[1])\cong(QK)[1]$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $Lu^*:D(R)\to D(S)$, with its shift isomorphisms $\sigma_X:Lu^*(X[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(Lu^*X)[1]$ and its canonical comparison $\epsilon:Lu^*Q_R\to Q_Su^*$, be the exact derived pullback of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Then: (1) $\epsilon$ commutes with shifts: for every complex $P$ of $R$-modules, $\epsilon_{P[1]}$ equals $\epsilon_P[1]\circ\sigma_{Q_RP}$ after the shift isomorphisms of $Q_R$ and $Q_S$ and the identity $u^*(P[1])=(u^*P)[1]$. (2) Let $0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ be a degreewise short exact sequence of cochain complexes of $R$-modules, each of which is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Then $0\to u^*A\to u^*B\to u^*C\to0$ is degreewise short exact. Let $\delta:Q_RC\to(Q_RA)[1]$ and $\delta':Q_Su^*C\to(Q_Su^*A)[1]$ be the canonical boundaries of these two sequences [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle], namely $\delta=-Q(p)\circ Q(q)^{-1}$, where $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^r=B^r\oplus A^{r+1}$ with differential $(x,a)\mapsto(d_Bx+f(a),-d_Aa)$, $q:\operatorname{Cone}(f)\to C$ is induced by $g$ and $p:\operatorname{Cone}(f)\to A[1]$ is the projection, and likewise for $\delta'$ with $u^*f,u^*g$. Then $(\epsilon_A,\epsilon_B,\epsilon_C)$ is an isomorphism of triangles from
$$Lu^*Q_RA\xrightarrow{Lu^*Q_Rf}Lu^*Q_RB\xrightarrow{Lu^*Q_Rg}Lu^*Q_RC\xrightarrow{\sigma_{Q_RA}\circ Lu^*(\delta)}(Lu^*Q_RA)[1]$$
to $Q_Su^*A\xrightarrow{Q_Su^*f}Q_Su^*B\xrightarrow{Q_Su^*g}Q_Su^*C\xrightarrow{\delta'}(Q_Su^*A)[1]$; in particular $\epsilon_A[1]\circ\sigma_{Q_RA}\circ Lu^*(\delta)=\delta'\circ\epsilon_C$. No boundedness of the complexes and no flatness of $u$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $T=u^*$ and $F=Q_ST:K(R)\to D(S)$. Exact geometric inverse image is additive. Tensor is additive on morphisms by its bilinear relations and preserves finite coproducts by the tensor-colimits lemma, so $T$ is additive. Applying $T$ to a chain homotopy preserves the equation $h d+d h$, hence defines the indicated functor on homotopy categories. The biproduct comparison gives $T\operatorname{Cone}(a)\cong\operatorname{Cone}(Ta)$: in degree $r$ both differentials are the matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}T(d)&T(a)\\0&-T(d)\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. It identifies inclusions, projections and their negatives. Also $T(P[1])\cong(TP)[1]$ has differential $-T(d_P)$. Thus $F$ commutes with shifts and sends cone triangles to cone triangles, and is exact by the cone description of the triangulation.

proof.text: Take $\mathcal P$ to be the flat-term K-flat complexes. The K-flat-resolution lemma supplies a quasi-isomorphism from an object of $\mathcal P$ to every complex. The ringed-topoi-derived-pullback lemma states that $T$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms between these complexes. Therefore the resolving-class criterion, applied to the exact $F$ of step 1, supplies the right Kan universal property of $(Lu^*,\epsilon)$; this is the canonical derived pair, identified by its universal comparison. Apply the coherent-shift theorem for right Kan extensions to $Q_R,F,Lu^*,\epsilon$. Its conclusion says precisely that the canonical shifts of the derived functor make $\epsilon$ shift-compatible. With the localization shift identifications and the termwise shift identification of step 1 this reads $\epsilon_{P[1]}=\epsilon_P[1]\circ\sigma_{Q_RP}$. This proves (1) for every complex $P$, without any K-flatness assumption on $P$.

proof.text: Fix a degree $r$. Exactness of geometric inverse image gives $0\to u^{-1}A^r\to u^{-1}B^r\to u^{-1}C^r\to0$ over $u^{-1}R$. Apply flat-module pullback to the ringed-topos morphism $(u,u^{-1}R)$ with coefficient map $\mathrm{id}_{u^{-1}R}$: since $C^r$ is flat, $u^{-1}C^r$ is flat over $u^{-1}R$. The flat-quotient sheaf tensor lemma with $N=S$ now makes this sequence short exact after tensoring with $S$. Tensor symmetry identifies it with $0\to TA^r\to TB^r\to TC^r\to0$, so the image complex sequence is degreewise short exact. In particular this uses flatness of the quotient terms, not flatness of $S$ over $u^{-1}R$.

Set $V=\operatorname{Cone}(f)$ and $V'=\operatorname{Cone}(Tf)$. The cone-projection quasi-isomorphism lemma, applied to the original sequence and the sequence of step 3, makes $q:V\to C$ and $q':V'\to TC$ quasi-isomorphisms. Hence $Q_Rq,Q_Sq'$ are invertible. Write $h:TV\xrightarrow{\sim}V'$ for the strict cone identification of step 1. Directly on the two summands, $q'h=Tq$ and $p'h=Tp$, where shifts are identified. Thus $Fq=Q_S(q'h)$ is invertible too. By the definitions of the two boundaries in the statement, $\delta=-Q_Rp\,(Q_Rq)^{-1}$ and $\delta'=-Q_Sp'\,(Q_Sq')^{-1}$. Each is the cone triangle's last map transported along its cone projection, so these are distinguished triangles by the cone-induced triangulation; this also fixes the same minus sign on both sides.

source.place: Section 014Z (section-canonical-delta-functor), paragraphs preceding Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor): q and the boundary -p q^{-1}

proof.text:
Naturality of $\epsilon$ at $p:V\to A[1]$ and $q:V\to C$ gives $\epsilon_{A[1]}Lu^*(Q_Rp)=Fp\,\epsilon_V$ and $\epsilon_C Lu^*(Q_Rq)=Fq\,\epsilon_V$. Since $Q_Rq$ and $Fq$ are invertible, the second equation gives $\epsilon_V Lu^*((Q_Rq)^{-1})=(Fq)^{-1}\epsilon_C$. Substituting these equations and step 2 into the prescribed boundary yields
$$\epsilon_A[1]\,\sigma_{Q_RA}\,Lu^*(\delta)=-Fp\,(Fq)^{-1}\epsilon_C=-Q_Sp'\,(Q_Sq')^{-1}\epsilon_C=\delta'\epsilon_C.$$
The middle equality cancels $Q_Sh$ using $Fp=Q_S(p'h)$ and $Fq=Q_S(q'h)$ from step 4. Additivity preserves the minus sign. Naturality at $f,g$ gives the other two squares. Finally the ringed-topoi-derived-pullback lemma makes $\epsilon_A,\epsilon_B,\epsilon_C$ invertible, since all three complexes are flat-term K-flat. These three squares and three isomorphisms are the asserted triangle isomorphism. Exactness of $Lu^*$ makes its source triangle distinguished. No inverse to $\epsilon_V$, no boundedness, and no flatness of $u$ was used.

lean.note: The universal derived pair is expressed on cochain complexes, as in the item, using Q rather than Qh. Restriction along the homotopy quotient identifies this with the dependency’s universal pair via quotientCompQhIso. The existential CommShift structure is the canonical comparison-compatible shift: the first conjunct explicitly pins its [1] comparison on every complex. No arbitrary exact shift or exactness of the underived pullback is assumed.
